citation: Ali, Orfi, and Najib (2020), Developing and validating a dynamic model of water production by direct-contact membrane distillation
study_type: First-principles transient mass-production model (lumped and spatial) with experimental step-response validation
system_scope: 10 m² spiral-wound counter-current DCMD; 50, 100, 200, 300 L/h; nominal 50–80 °C step cases; 10-second measurements of accumulated distillate mass
empirical_data_or_code: Five publisher-listed XLSX files acquired and SHA-256 pinned; 17,385 transient records and 16 steady-state conditions extracted; see docs/ALI_2020_SUPPORTING_DATA_AUDIT_2026-10-13.md
source_supported_finding: Paper derives a dynamic mass-production equation coupled to hot/cold outlet-temperature ODEs and an iterative pseudo-steady membrane-interface solver. Untuned overall relative errors are 11.02% (lumped) and 18.52% (spatial); reported errors fall to 3.22% and 3.25% only after a flow-dependent heuristic heat-loss/model-error correction. The authors explicitly describe the correction as trial-and-error/heuristic.
relevance_to_this_project: Useful independent-study dynamic dataset for evaluating a separately implemented model and input-response handling. The source's tuned results are a reproduction target, not independent validation.
limitation_or_non_claim: Dynamic DCMD mass-production modeling and transient experimental validation are prior art. Do not claim the first dynamic DCMD model or first transient mass-flux model. The fitted correction absorbs both heat losses and other modeling error; preserve untuned/tuned results separately and do not use tuned cases as held-out evidence.
license_or_reuse_note: CC BY 4.0 per publisher; five source XLSX hashes and generated ledger hashes are recorded in the repository. Attribute source and document modifications.
